items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: suggesting a Cannonball tune to one of my students

ctx.x: know layer it up and send it out and there it goes and you know nobody over the age of 18 has heard it before, it’s just heading out there. You know so I think that’s what I meant, just to make sure that even though there might be avenues — a lot more avenues open to putting your music out there, to make sure you’re being very critical of yourself and you know, attending to the best practices for learning to play, learning to compose.

As a teacher, do you find that you need to try and guide students through their choices on an endless smorgasbord of things that they can listen to? I guess what I’m after is I remember years ago when this whole thing — everything is available — was just starting and suggesting a Cannonball tune to one of my students and it was sort of like, “Oh yes I’ve heard that on YouTube, I heard it on YouTube.” And I just got — the way he said it seemed to be like, “Yeah and I’ve heard everything else that you’re about to…

It’s a well founded observation, yeah. We talk to our students about — do you just have — you know your headphones are on almost continually but are you multi-tasking? What else are you doing when you’re (I’m using air quotes here) “listening” to the music? You know and do you have it on at your house while you’re doing ten million other things? So yeah, we talk a lot about the need to do deep listening. And that’s why we’re still forcing transcriptions and things like that. You know I give assignments where I…
